Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/18/2025
Patient: Casey Schiller, 77 y/o M

Attended PSG 04/18/2025. Study completed without complications. Sleep efficiency 78%. Total sleep time 345 min. REM latency 110 min. AHI 32.4/h. CA+MA 16% of total AHI. Oxygen nadir 84%. Periodic limb movements index 5/h. No significant arrhythmias noted. CPAP titration recommended given severity of obstructive events. Further clinical correlation advised.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/25/2026
Patient: Casey Schiller, 78 y.o. M

Hx: OSA dx 2018, CPAP tx started 2019. Pt reports persistent daytime fatigue, nonrestorative sleep.

CPAP dl avg 3.2 h/night, 41% nights despite mask refit; SDM w/ pt: CPAP intolerant.

Nocturnal oximetry shows intermittent desats to 85%. Pt uses CPAP sporadically, reports mask discomfort and nasal congestion.

Plan: Consider alternative therapies including oral appliance or positional therapy. Sleep hygiene reinforced. Follow-up PSG to reassess severity and response to new interventions.

Pt advised on risks of untreated OSA. Next appt in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Otolaryngology Consultation
Date: 09/24/2026
Patient: Casey Schiller, 78yo M

77yo M referred for HGNS eval. Pt c/o snoring, witnessed apnea. PMH noncontributory. Exam: Tonsils 1+, no other obstruction. Nasal passages patent. Oral cavity unremarkable.

DISE 09/09/2026: AP velum collapse, no CCC. Hypopharynx patent. No tongue base obstruction.

Plan: Consider HGNS candidacy. Discussed potential benefits and risks. Will arrange sleep study follow-up and coordinate with pulmonology for further management.
